answer.summary: Rahul Vohra’s Switch log records what he actually works on, rather than what his calendar planned: whenever he switches tasks, he sends a short “TS:” note to his EA or a Slackbot, then reviews the log at week’s end.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.content: Vohra says a calendar shows what you thought you would do, while your trail of work shows what you actually did. His technique is to work on what feels right, and each time he changes tasks, Slack DM his EA—or send the note to a Slackbot—with “TS:” followed by a few words describing the task. At the end of the week, he reviews where his time went; the log can also be graphed and charted. He clarifies that this does not mean skipping meetings or one-on-ones.

judgment.explanation: The answer accurately explains that the Switch log captures actual work rather than calendar plans and that Vohra logs each task change with a brief “TS:” note to his EA or a Slackbot. The cited context also supports reviewing and charting the log later. It answers the question without claiming that relevant information is missing.
